column1: # log_mask.tsv — free text said with every credential in it hidden: the platform's `secrets.mask_text`, outside any
# spec (the product's decision, 5 Oct). A log line, an error a driver said, a request it logged, a JSON document. Seeded
# from the free-text rows of the product's draft of secret_in.tsv (wt-boundary-4b), then the course's own.
# Columns, tab-separated, one row a line; a line that begins with '#' and an empty line are no row:
#   masked  what is said of it: every password, token or key masked as *** where it stands; a login left as written
#   note    why the row is here
# The reader masks by the platform's own names of a credential alone (`secrets.COMMON_RULES`), no spec's.

column3: a connect string: the value runs to the end — more masked, never less
an empty value stays empty: not set is no secret
an address in a JSON text ends at its quote
a port followed by what closes a sentence is a number
a driver's RTSP client logs its request
a JSON member named as a credential; a login's is left
a log line: the userinfo's login said, its password not
a command line a driver logged
names of their own: no credential's word, whole or last
=pin the whole name, key the last word
